docs.title: Honest Practice
docs.text:
A desk for daily practice. Each day the system publishes five new DSA patterns and five new system design patterns, drawn from public writing on the web, and it refuses to publish a pattern it has already given you. You can read any earlier edition, ask an assistant about a pattern, and define further tasks of the same kind.

This repository is at Phase 0. The API answers /health, a worker process stays running, and this page is the map of the documentation that the later phases fill in.

docs.title: 0.1.0 — 2026-10-23
docs.text:
Phase 0 skeleton.

  • Python package honest_practice with settings, a /health route, and an idle worker.
  • Next.js page that reports API health.
  • Docker Compose services for Postgres (pgvector), the API, the worker, and the web app.
  • Documentation tree, MkDocs site, and architecture decisions 0001–0006.
  • CI for lint, types, tests, import boundaries, the docs build, and the frontend.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Phase 0 is a skeleton. Contributions that add a feature from a later phase should land in that phase's shape, not as a shortcut through it.

docs.title: Before you open a change
docs.text:
• Read module boundaries if the change adds an import.
  • Read commenting if the change adds a public function.
  • Update the document that describes the behaviour you changed. An outline page can stay an outline. A page that states a fact has to stay true. ADR-0005 is the reason.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv run --directory backend ruff check src tests
uv run --directory backend ruff format --check src tests
uv run --directory backend mypy
uv run --directory backend lint-imports
uv run --directory backend pytest
uv run --directory backend mkdocs build --strict --config-file ../mkdocs.yml
pnpm --dir frontend lint
pnpm --dir frontend typecheck
pnpm --dir frontend format:check
pnpm --dir frontend build

CI runs the same list. A red check is fixed in a new commit, not by skipping the hook.

docs.title: Commits
docs.text: Use a short imperative message that says why the change exists. git log is the style guide once there is history. Do not commit .env, key files, or the site/ build.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: A change that picks a direction the next person would otherwise have to guess at gets a new ADR under docs/03-architecture/adr/. Do not rewrite an accepted record to say something else. Supersede it.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Honest Practice is one repository: a Python backend, a Next.js frontend, and this documentation tree.

The backend is the package honest_practice. The frontend is the pnpm workspace under frontend/. Docker Compose in deploy/ runs Postgres, the API, the worker, and the web app together.

If you are new, read the quickstart, then the reading map. If you are about to change a boundary between packages, read module boundaries before you write the import.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: These steps start the Phase 0 system on your machine: Postgres, the API, the worker, and the web page.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Docker, with Compose v2
  • Nothing else. The images build the Python and Node toolchains themselves

For working on the code without Docker, you also need Python 3.12, uv, Node.js 22, and pnpm 10.21.0. The frontend package.json pins that pnpm release. Corepack will use it when packageManager is set.

docs.title: Start the stack
docs.text:
From the repository root:

docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build

Then open:

  • Web: http://localhost:3000
  • API health: http://localhost:8000/health
  • API docs (generated by FastAPI): http://localhost:8000/docs

/health returns HTTP 200 when the API can run SELECT 1 against Postgres. The page at port 3000 reads that endpoint from the browser and shows "API ready".

Copy .env.example to .env only when you want to override a default. Compose runs without that file. See configuration.

docs.title: Work on the backend
docs.text:
uv sync --directory backend --group dev
uv run --directory backend pytest
uv run --directory backend uvicorn honest_practice.api.app:app --reload --port 8000

Postgres still has to be running. The compose file can start it on its own:

docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up postgres

The default database URL points at localhost:5432 with user, password, and database all set to honest_practice.

docs.title: Work on the frontend
docs.text:
pnpm install --dir frontend
pnpm --dir frontend dev

The dev server uses http://localhost:8000 unless NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL is set. That variable is read when the production image is built, not at request time.

docs.title: Build the docs
docs.text:
uv run --directory backend mkdocs build --strict --config-file ../mkdocs.yml

The site is written to site/. To read it while editing:

uv run --directory backend mkdocs serve --config-file ../mkdocs.yml

mkdocs is a backend development dependency, which is why the command runs through uv in backend/ while the config file stays at the repository root.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Honest Practice is one deployable system with three processes: a web app, an API, and a worker. They share one Postgres database. The worker is the only process that calls the Cursor SDK and the only process that fetches web pages.

flowchart LR
  browser[Browser]
  web[Web]
  api[API]
  worker[Worker]
  db[("Postgres")]
  cursor[CursorSDK]
  sites[PublicWeb]
  browser --> web
  browser --> api
  web --> api
  api --> db
  worker --> db
  worker --> cursor
  worker --> sites

The browser talks to the API directly for health, and later for editions and tasks. The web server does not proxy those calls in Phase 0. That is why NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL is a public URL and why the API has a CORS list.

docs.title: Module boundaries
docs.text:
The backend is one installable package, honest_practice, with subpackages that are not allowed to import each other freely. The rules live in backend/pyproject.toml under [tool.importlinter] and run in CI as lint-imports.

A rule that is only written down will be broken. A rule that fails the build will be discussed first.

docs.title: The packages
docs.text:
Package May import Must not import core The standard library and third-party libraries that do no I/O for us Every other honest_practice subpackage agents, sources, memory, uniqueness, db core, and each other when a later phase needs it api, worker, cli tasks core and the adapter packages api. The worker calls tasks, not the other way around api core, adapter packages, tasks worker worker core, adapter packages, tasks api cli The same services the API uses, once they exist api

config and logging sit at the package root. Every process may import them. They are not a place to hide a database call.

docs.title: The three contracts
docs.text:
1. Core stays free of I/O and adapters. honest_practice.core cannot import agents, sources, memory, uniqueness, tasks, db, api, worker, or cli.
  2. Adapters do not depend on delivery. agents, sources, memory, uniqueness, and db cannot import api, worker, or cli.
  3. API and worker are independent. Neither imports the other. They share behaviour by calling a lower package.

docs.title: How to add a package
docs.text: Add the directory, give it a module docstring that says what it owns and what it must not import, and add it to the contract that matches that sentence. If you cannot name the contract, the package boundary is not decided yet. Write the decision down before the code.

docs.title: Why this shape
docs.text: ADR-0002 records the choice of one package plus a linter, instead of many separately versioned packages.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
An architecture decision record is a short note of a choice and the reason for it. We keep them so a later change can see what it is undoing.

Records are numbered and are not edited to match a new decision. A replacement gets a new number and marks the old one superseded.

Record Status Choice 0001 Accepted Python API, Next.js UI, Postgres with pgvector 0002 Accepted One Python package, boundaries checked by import-linter 0003 Accepted Queue and schedules in Postgres, no Redis 0004 Accepted TypeScript client generated from the OpenAPI schema 0005 Accepted One Markdown tree, three ways to read it 0006 Accepted Memory changes context. Uniqueness always uses full history

docs.title: ADR-0001: Stack
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Honest Practice has to do four kinds of work: serve a learner's interface, run a daily pipeline, call the Cursor SDK, and remember years of patterns well enough to refuse duplicates. The pipeline is unattended. The interface is something a person reads every day, so it is a real web app and not a notebook.

The Cursor SDK exists for Python and TypeScript. The person building this chose Python for the backend, local development first, and a documented path onto a VPS later.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, and uv for the backend.
  • SQLAlchemy 2.0 and Alembic against Postgres 16 with the pgvector image. Vectors are how later phases compare a new pattern with the archive.
  • Next.js (App Router) and TypeScript for the frontend, in a pnpm workspace.
  • The cursor-sdk async client, called from one gateway module. Phase 2 writes that module. The runtime is set explicitly to local.
  • Docker Compose for local runs. A production profile with a reverse proxy and single-user authentication is Phase 12, recorded here so the local file does not grow production concerns by accident.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Two languages. The API schema is the contract between them, which ADR-0004 makes mechanical.
  • Postgres is a hard dependency, including for local development. Compose starts it.
  • The Python SDK's async client must be the only client in the process. Mixing the sync client and the async client is a known footgun and the gateway will not do it.
  • Model calls cost money. Budget fields exist in settings now (HP_BUDGET_PER_RUN_USD, HP_BUDGET_PER_DAY_USD) so Phase 2 has a place to enforce them.

docs.title: ADR-0002: One package, checked boundaries
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The backend has a domain (patterns, editions, tasks), adapters (database, web sources, the Cursor SDK, memory), and two delivery processes (API and worker). Splitting those into separately published Python packages would make the dependency direction obvious and the day-to-day workflow heavier: more lockfiles, more version bumps, more empty packages to release for a solo project.

Leaving them as one package with no rules makes the dependency direction a suggestion.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Ship one package, honest_practice, laid out by responsibility under backend/src/honest_practice/. Encode the allowed imports as import-linter contracts in backend/pyproject.toml, and fail CI when a contract breaks.

core imports no other subpackage. Adapter packages do not import api, worker, or cli. api and worker do not import each other.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A new seam is a new subpackage plus a contract, not a new project.
  • The linter sees imports, not runtime calls. A boundary can still be violated by reaching through a string import. Reviewers treat that as the same violation.
  • Tests may import any package. The contracts apply to honest_practice itself.
  • The layout is documented in module boundaries. That page and the contracts must move together.

docs.title: ADR-0003: Postgres is the queue
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Scheduled tasks and manual runs need a queue with retries, and a scheduler that reads those schedules. Adding Redis would give a familiar queue and a second service to back up, secure, and explain. The system already requires Postgres. Runs are not high-frequency: a handful of editions a day, plus crawls and the occasional manual trigger.

The product also requires that anything the scheduler can run, a person can run by hand. That is a property of the trigger path, not of the queue technology. It is recorded here so Phase 5 does not grow a second implementation for manual runs.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Procrastinate, which stores jobs in Postgres, is the queue.
  • APScheduler reads task rows and asks one TriggerService to enqueue a job.
  • The API, the CLI, and the web UI call that same service. A run records its trigger: schedule, manual_ui, manual_cli, api, or retry.
  • No Redis in local Compose and none in the production profile.

Phase 5 builds this. Phase 0 only keeps a worker process alive so the Compose service exists.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One database to back up. Job state is in the same backup as editions.
  • Throughput is bounded by Postgres. That is acceptable at this volume. A later record can revisit it if a crawl fan-out proves otherwise.
  • The worker must be running for a manual trigger to finish. The API enqueues. It does not do the work inline.
  • Schedules and jobs share a failure domain with the database. If Postgres is down, nothing runs, and /health says so.

docs.title: ADR-0004: Generate the TypeScript client from OpenAPI
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The frontend and the backend are different languages. Hand-written types drift. The health response is small enough to write by hand, and Phase 0 does that, in @honest-practice/api-client. The API that follows (editions, tasks, runs, jobs) is not.

FastAPI already publishes an OpenAPI schema.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Phase 6 generates frontend/api-client from that schema with openapi-typescript. CI checks the schema, regenerates the client, and fails if the committed file differs.

Until Phase 6, the hand-written health type is allowed. New endpoints do not get hand-written twins. They wait for the generator, or they arrive in the same change as the generator.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The schema is a product artifact. Renaming a field is a frontend change, and the diff shows it.
  • Generation runs in CI, so a missing Python extra or a changed tool version fails in the open.
  • The client package stays free of UI code. The web app imports types and, later, request functions. It does not re-declare responses.

docs.title: ADR-0005: One documentation tree, three readers
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The docs have to serve three readers: someone in the repository, someone browsing a site, and the learner inside the app. Three copies would disagree within a month. The docs also have to stay long enough to be the reference for the system, which makes drift expensive.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Markdown under docs/ is the only source.
  • MkDocs Material builds the browsable site from that tree. mkdocs build --strict is part of CI, so a broken link or a file missing from the nav fails the build.
  • Phase 8 renders the same files in the app. It does not keep a second set.
  • Reference pages that can be generated (Python API, environment names, database schema, HTTP API) are generated from code in later phases. Phase 0 starts that habit for environment variables: environment_variable_names() is the list, docs/10-reference/environment.md must mention each name, and a test checks.

Pages that describe unbuilt behaviour are outlines. They name the phase that fills them. They do not describe the feature as if it already runs.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A behaviour change updates the page in the same change. The contributing guide says so.
  • The app and the site can differ in chrome (navigation, fonts) and must not differ in words.
  • Strict mode means a new page is not done until it is in mkdocs.yml.
  • Outlines are allowed to be short. Inventing the future in detail, before the code, is how this tree goes stale.

docs.title: ADR-0006: Memory changes context, not uniqueness
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-23

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
A task can run with memory on or off. On means the agent may see earlier patterns, notes, and study progress. Off means it sees the sources for this run and the task instructions, and nothing from the archive.

The same product promises that a new edition does not repeat a pattern you already have. If "memory off" also meant "do not look at history when deciding what is new", a fresh-start run could republish last month's pattern under a new title. That would make the toggle a way to break the promise.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Memory policy chooses the context builder:

  • none passes no archive context.
  • history_summary passes a compressed list of past titles, topics, and study progress.
  • vector_retrieval passes related past patterns and notes.

Uniqueness always runs against the full history of that pattern kind: exact slug, then embedding similarity, then an LLM judge only for the borderline band. The memory setting is not an input to that check.

A manual run may override memory for that run. The override is stored on the run. It is not stored back onto the task, and it does not skip uniqueness.

Phase 4 implements the check. This record exists now so the setting is not designed as a single "use history" flag that means both things.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• "Fresh start" is about the agent's reading, not about amnesia in the archive.
  • Uniqueness has to be cheap enough to run on every generation, including dry runs. The LLM judge is limited to the borderline band for that reason.
  • The run ledger records the memory policy that was actually used, so a past edition can be explained.
  • A bug that wires memory policy into the uniqueness query is a violation of this decision, not a feature.

docs.title: Failure and retry

docs.title: Commenting
docs.text: Comments and documents do different jobs. The document says what the system is for and how the pieces fit. The comment says what a reader of this function cannot see from the next ten lines.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
Public modules, classes, and functions use Google-style docstrings. Ruff's D rules, with the Google convention, enforce that in CI.

A docstring includes:

  • a summary line that says what the callable is for, not a restatement of its name
  • Args when there is an argument worth explaining
  • Returns when the return value is not obvious from the summary
  • a note of errors the caller is expected to handle, when the function raises them

Do not add a docstring that repeats the signature in prose. Do not add a comment above a line that says what the line does.

def check_database(database_url: str) -> str:
    """Run ``SELECT 1`` and report the outcome without raising.

    The returned string never includes the URL, because the URL contains
    the database password.

    Args:
        database_url: SQLAlchemy URL, including the driver.

    Returns:
        ``ok``, or ``error:`` plus the exception class name.
    """

An inline comment is for a constraint: a timeout, an ordering requirement, a workaround, a reason a value looks arbitrary. The health check sets a connect timeout because a down database must not hold the probe open. That is worth a comment. status_code = 200 is not.

docs.title: TypeScript
docs.text: Exported functions, types, and components get a TSDoc comment with the same standard: purpose, and anything the types do not say. HealthResponse documents that HTTP 503 uses the same body as HTTP 200, because the type system cannot say that.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Process configuration is the Settings class in backend/src/honest_practice/config.py. If a value is not a field there, the process does not read it. The names and the descriptions are listed in the environment reference. A test fails when a field is missing from that page.

docs.title: Where values come from
docs.text:
1. Environment variables.
  2. A .env file at the repository root, or backend/.env if you keep one there. The repository-root file wins when both exist, because it is listed first. Docker images do not contain either file.
  3. The defaults on the field.

Copy .env.example to .env to start from the defaults in a file you can edit. .env is gitignored.

Compose sets HP_DATABASE_URL itself for the API and the worker, so those containers talk to the postgres service even if your .env points at localhost.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
Most variables use the prefix HP_. The Cursor SDK looks for CURSOR_API_KEY, so that name is accepted as well as HP_CURSOR_API_KEY.

HP_CORS_ORIGINS is a JSON list, for example ["http://localhost:3000"].

docs.title: Secrets in logs
docs.text: database_url and cursor_api_key are redacted. Settings.for_log() prints set or unset for them and never the value. The worker logs that mapping at startup. Do not log settings itself.

docs.title: Changing a default
docs.text: Add or edit the field, document the variable in the environment reference, and mention the reason in the field's docstring. The docstring is the explanation a caller of get_settings() sees. The reference is the explanation an operator sees.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: Phase 0 runs as four Compose services. Later phases add behaviour inside the same services.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service Image Port on the host Role postgres pgvector/pgvector:pg16 5432 Database. pgvector is unused until embeddings arrive api Built from backend/Dockerfile 8000 FastAPI. Health check calls /health worker Same image, command python -m honest_practice.worker none Idle heartbeat until Phase 5 web Built from frontend/Dockerfile 3000 Next.js page

The Compose project name is honest-practice.

docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build

Stop it with docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml down. The database volume pgdata survives down. down -v deletes it.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
The API is healthy when /health returns HTTP 200. That requires Postgres to answer SELECT 1. Compose waits for pg_isready before starting the API, then waits for /health before starting the web container.

A failed database check returns HTTP 503 and a body whose checks.database is error: plus an exception class name. The body does not contain the database URL.

docs.title: Tools for local development
docs.text:
Tool Version used here What for Python 3.12 Backend. backend/.python-version pins it for uv uv 0.9.x Backend installs and the lockfile Node.js 22 Frontend pnpm 10.21.0, pinned in frontend/package.json Frontend workspace. pnpm 12 rejects the lockfile under its release-age policy

Commands are in the quickstart.

docs.text:

  • No Redis, no separate queue process. See ADR-0003.
  • The worker does not dequeue anything yet.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text: Phase 0 exposes one route. FastAPI also serves its own schema UI at /docs and the schema at /openapi.json. Those are framework routes, not product routes, and Phase 6 will decide which of them stay available in production.

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Reports whether the process can serve traffic.

HTTP 200 when every enabled check passed. HTTP 503 when any check failed. The body shape is the same in both cases.

{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "honest-practice",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "checks": {
    "api": "ok",
    "database": "ok"
  }
}
Field Values status ok or degraded service Always honest-practice version The backend version in pyproject.toml checks.api ok when this function ran checks.database ok, skipped, or error: plus an exception class name

checks.database is skipped when HP_HEALTH_CHECK_DATABASE is false. The error value does not include the database URL.

CORS allows the origins in HP_CORS_ORIGINS. The Phase 0 page calls this route from the browser.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
The names below come from environment_variable_names() in honest_practice.config. Adding a field without mentioning its name here fails tests/test_project.py.

Defaults are the field defaults. Compose overrides HP_DATABASE_URL inside containers. See configuration.

docs.title: Process
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose HP_ENVIRONMENT local local or production. Production is for the Phase 12 profile. HP_LOG_LEVEL INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, or ERROR.

docs.title: API
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose HP_API_HOST 0.0.0.0 Bind address inside the container. HP_API_PORT 8000 Bind port inside the container. HP_CORS_ORIGINS ["http://localhost:3000"] JSON list of browser origins allowed to call the API.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose HP_DATABASE_URL postgresql+psycopg://honest_practice:honest_practice@localhost:5432/honest_practice SQLAlchemy URL. Never logged. HP_HEALTH_CHECK_DATABASE true When true, /health runs SELECT 1.

docs.title: Cursor SDK
docs.text:
Used from Phase 2. Present now so the gateway has one place to read them.

Variable Default Purpose CURSOR_API_KEY empty Credential the SDK reads. Also accepted as HP_CURSOR_API_KEY. Never logged. HP_CURSOR_API_KEY empty Same value, prefixed form. HP_CURSOR_MODEL composer-2.5 Model id passed to the SDK. HP_CURSOR_RUNTIME local local or cloud. The gateway will set this explicitly and will not assume a default. HP_AGENT_SANDBOX_DIR /var/lib/honest-practice/sandbox Working directory for a local agent, outside this repository.

docs.title: Budgets and editions
docs.text:
Enforced from Phase 2 and Phase 4. The fields exist so those phases do not invent a second configuration object.

Variable Default Purpose HP_BUDGET_PER_RUN_USD 1.0 Soft cap for one run. HP_BUDGET_PER_DAY_USD 5.0 Soft cap for a calendar day. A manual run past this cap asks for confirmation. HP_EDITION_PATTERN_COUNT 5 How many unique patterns one edition publishes.

docs.title: Worker
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose HP_WORKER_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS 30 How often the Phase 0 worker logs that it is idle. Minimum 5, maximum 3600.

docs.title: Frontend build
docs.text:
Not part of Settings. The Next.js image reads it when the image is built.

Variable Default Purpose NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL http://localhost:8000 URL the browser uses to call the API.
